Hey — the place is ready: a TypeScript pnpm monorepo with a server, a web app, and an OpenClaw client package.
What should we work on? You can also tell me how you like to work and I'll remember it.

I'm root, the coordinator for this project (ArbosClaw). I keep track of goals and progress, route substantial work to workers, and combine their results — you talk to me, and I make sure the work gets done and reported back. Tell me what to build or fix and I'll get it moving.
how do you organize your project
how do you organize your project

Everything lives in the `.arbos/` folder next to your code, in a few plain files:

- `docs/project-context.md` — the standing brief: your goal, constraints, and dated decisions. I write it the moment you state one, so it's the one place to check what we agreed.
- `notes.md` — the project page: one checkbox per workstream with a live status, linking to whatever it produced (a PR, a document). Finished items sink into `archived.md`.
- `docs/` — deliverables you asked for (plans, research writeups); `media/` — screenshots and recordings; `internal/` — handoff notes between agents that you'll rarely need.

Code changes go through workers: each fix lands on its own branch and opens as a draft PR against `main`, never a commit on `main` itself, and nothing gets merged unless you say so. Preferences you tell me about how to work are saved to memory and apply going forward.
